narrative:
The model estimated a 63% probability that you would represent a bad credit risk, meaning that among applicants with a similar financial profile, about 63 in 100 were predicted to have repayment difficulty. Because this exceeded the bank’s approval threshold, your application was denied.

The strongest factor increasing your risk assessment was your checking account position. Your account is in the 0–200 DM range, while most approved applicants have no checking account at all and only about 18% fall into this range; this made your profile look less secure. The second most influential factor was the absence of recorded property. Only about 8% of approved applicants have unknown or no property, while most show a car, real estate, or building-society/life-insurance assets, so this lack of collateral or asset information added materially to the risk view. The third factor was the requested duration: you asked for 36 months, well above the approved average of roughly 19 months, and a longer commitment increased the model’s concern. These three factors all pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Next, ask the bank what documentation could strengthen a future application. Consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, providing evidence of savings, assets, or collateral, and building a more stable checking and savings history. If available, a guarantor or co-applicant may also help. Reapplying after these areas improve would give the model a stronger profile to assess.
